span.p:
p_pool = pooled proportion
se_pool = sqrt(p_pool*(1-p_pool)*(1/n1+1/n2))
z = (p2-p1) / se_pool

span.p:
scipy.stats.ttest_ind(
treatment, control, equal_var=False)
— Welch's, NOT Student's

span.p:
significant_at_05 =
bool(p_value < 0.05)
(explicit bool() —
numpy bool caused a real
test bug before this fix)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Result: SIGNIFICANT
— the observed difference is
unlikely to be chance

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Result: NOT significant
— could be noise, even if the
raw lift number LOOKS big

p_value is NaN?
(e.g. zero-variance
identical samples)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
nan < 0.05 evaluates False in Python
→ NEVER falsely claims significance
(the fail-safe direction)
